scope: Historical v4 source-rights audit of 72 names from the older 38-portrait brief. Not the current site lookup or to-do list.
search_limitations: Targeted search, not exhaustive. Many hits are objects or namesakes. Queries can return only the first 25 matches; more_results_available flags truncated results. Openverse filtered searches were unavailable and were not counted as successful negatives.

people.name: Andrée Tretiakoff
people.context: Patented braille dots raised by piezoelectric reeds. They filed first in France, in 1974.
people.v4_findings: No named portrait tied to the braille co-inventor was found in this pass. Exact-name and unaccented-name Commons searches returned no files. The ACL author page has no portrait; it does not identify an otherwise anonymous sitter.

people.name: Elma Farnsworth
people.context: Known as Pem. She worked beside Philo Farnsworth in his laboratories, and her face was among the first that his system sent.
people.v4_findings: The named Television Academy interview still establishes identity, but its dim, soft frames remain insufficient for a convincing larger portrait. No open licence was verified for those frames or a replacement photo.

people.name: Vicki Colvin
people.context: Made an LED from quantum dots and a plastic that conducts, at the University of California, Berkeley. Colvin is the first author of the paper of 1994.
people.v4_findings: The Commons/Brown chronology conflict remains unresolved. A CC label from the uploader is not proof that the photographer or Brown authorised it. A separate Sandia photograph credited to Bill Doty was located, but no applicable open grant was verified. The round 3 study does not clear either photograph.

people.name: James Bryce
people.context: The IBM engineer. A British statesman, Viscount Bryce, shares the name.

Its exact embedded photograph is 556×833; the native face measures about 49.6 px across. It is too small for a drawing. The book has a copyright notice and the specific historical photograph’s publication/rights history was not established. A larger archive scan and a documented rights basis are needed.

people.context: The first holographic video display was built in Benton's group at the MIT Media Lab in 1989. Jepsen's thesis of that year sets out its design.
people.v4_findings: Bentonheadshot.jpg claims own work with a date after Benton died, without a photographer or release. Its RGB derivative explicitly reports retouching and replacement of missing areas. Neither was treated as a newly cleared source. The MIT Arts photo used in round 3 clips the crown and has no verified open grant.
